title: California Firm Acquires Film Rights to "The Emperor Wears No Clothes" -- Seeks Funding

content_html_sanitized:
NEWS RELEASE
January 22, 1998

Double J Films has acquired the documentary rights to the best-selling underground book "The Emperor Wears No Clothes" and is seeking investors to fund the low-budget production.

The book," authored by Jack Herer, is the bible of the cannabis/hemp movement. Part scientific treatise, part journalistic expose and part holy crusade, it reveals the lost history of cannabis/hemp and uncovers the facts behind marijuana prohibition. It's sold more than 600,000 copies since publication in 1985 and is currently in its 10th edition. High Times magazine calls the book "revolutionary."

"The Emperor Wears No Clothes - the Film" will be a detective story, a mystery about a man's passionate quest for the truth, says Producer Jeff Meyers.

"Jack Herer is a cult folk hero for almost single-handedly launching the worldwide grass-roots movement to unchain industrial hemp and legalize cannabis," Meyers says. "He did pioneering investigative reporting in writing the book. He discovered long-forgotten historical documents including items the government said didn't exist. We plan to let him tell the story on screen and convey the book through his experiences."

Meyers, a former Los Angeles Times staff writer, believes the documentary will appeal to a wide audience thanks to the medical marijuana issue, which has raised awareness of the drug's benefits among the once-disapproving masses, who no longer see marijuana as the demon weed.

"The general public is interested in marijuana history and intrigue, and the man who searched for the truth," Meyers says.

For further information, Meyers can be contacted at  jmeyers@isle.net.
